cls: Urinary antispasmodic (flavone smooth-muscle relaxant with anticholinergic activity)
pharm: Direct smooth-muscle relaxant of the urinary tract with mild anticholinergic and local anesthetic properties; relieves detrusor spasm and lower urinary tract symptoms.
quick: May take with or without food
Former Category B; use only if clearly needed
Symptom relief; caution if glaucoma suspected
summary: Flavoxate is a urinary tract antispasmodic for symptomatic relief of dysuria, urgency, frequency, nocturia, suprapubic pain, and incontinence due to cystitis, prostatitis, urethritis, urethrocystitis, or urethrotrigonitis. It acts directly on urinary smooth muscle to relieve spasm and has mild anticholinergic effects. It is not a definitive treatment of urinary tract infection but is compatible with antibiotics used for UTI. It is contraindicated in GI/urinary obstructive conditions and used cautiously in suspected glaucoma.
indications: Symptomatic relief of dysuria, urgency, nocturia, suprapubic pain, frequency, and incontinence
Symptoms occurring in cystitis, prostatitis, urethritis, urethrocystitis/urethrotrigonitis
Adjunct (not definitive therapy) alongside drugs treating urinary tract infections

dosage.n: Reduce dose as symptoms improve; not recommended under 12 years
Safety and efficacy not demonstrated in this age group

admin: Reduce the dose as symptoms improve
Do not use for definitive treatment of infection - pair with appropriate antimicrobial when indicated
Counsel patients about possible drowsiness/blurred vision before driving or operating machinery
moa: Counteracts smooth-muscle spasm of the urinary tract by acting directly on the muscle (papaverine-like myotropic relaxant), supplemented by mild anticholinergic, local anesthetic, and analgesic actions, thereby reducing detrusor overactivity and relieving urinary symptoms.

absolute: Obstructive uropathies of the lower urinary tract

preg: Former Pregnancy Category B - animal studies showed no fetal harm but adequate human studies are lacking; use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether flavoxate is excreted in human milk; exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is stated in the label; about 57% of a dose is excreted in urine within 24 hours.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is stated in the label.

moderate: Other anticholinergics (additive antimuscarinic effects - dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention)
minor: Drugs reduced in efficacy by anticholinergic GI slowing
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.

rare: Urticaria and other dermatoses, eosinophilia, hyperpyrexia

monitoring: Intraocular pressure if glaucoma is suspected
counsel: Take as prescribed for symptom relief; this treats symptoms, not the underlying infection
If drowsiness or blurred vision occurs, do not drive or operate machinery
Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or trouble passing urine/stool
Report rash, fever, or unusual bleeding/bruising
Dry mouth can be eased with sips of water or sugar-free gum
pk: Short; ~57% excreted in urine within 24 h
pearls: Provides symptomatic relief only - not a substitute for treating the underlying UTI
Compatible with antibiotics used for urinary tract infection
Contraindicated in GI and lower urinary tract obstructive conditions
Use cautiously in suspected glaucoma and in the elderly (confusion risk)
Mild anticholinergic burden - watch for additive effects with other antimuscarinics
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Symptoms reflect exaggerated anticholinergic/CNS effects. There is no specific antidote; provide symptomatic and supportive care. It is not known whether flavoxate is dialyzable. (Oral LD50 in rats 4273 mg/kg.)
